reaction_equations: N2 plasma -> cross-linking of phosphorous atoms
surface_mechanism_description: The ALD process involves sequential surface reactions where LiO tBu and H2O pulses lead to the formation of LiOH on the surface, followed by a ligand exchange reaction with TMP to form methyl phosphate species. Nitrogen plasma cross-linking occurs after the TMP pulse, which facilitates the amorphization of the film. The mechanism is summarized as: (a) Hydroxyl-terminated substrate; (b) Metastable surface after LiO tBu pulse; (c) H2O pulse removes tert-butanol ligands and forms LiOH; (d) TMP reacts with surface LiOH through ligand exchange, evolving CH3OH; (e) N2 plasma cross-links phosphorous atoms, evolving CH3OH and CH2O; (f) LiO tBu reacts with -OCH3 ligands, evolving both CH2OH and CH2O.
evidence: Scheme 1. Cartoon of the Proposed ALD LiPON Process Chemistry a (a) Hydroxyl terminated substrate; (b) metastable surface after the LiO tBu pulse; (c) H2O pulse removes the tert-butanol ligands and forms LiOH on the surface; (d) TMP reacts with surface LiOH through ligand exchange reaction, evolving CH3OH; (e) N2 plasma cross-links phosphorous atoms and evolve CH3OH and CH2O; (f) LiO tBu reacts with −OCH3 ligands and evolves both CH2OH and CH2O. The initial LiO tBu and H2O pulses shown in (a) and (b) are required “activate” the substrate prior to deposition. For all subsequent ALD cycles, the process chemistry in (c) through (f) is repeated as one ALD cycle.
